source.runnerFixUnderTest: The tested source 935bf8e contains two distinct runner commits. c1d65ff (935bf8e's parent) holds the remapped-pointer mouse return: after the keybinding save it re-reads the current canvas bounds (reboundBox) and issues a real page.mouse.move back into that canvas before the remapped F targeting check, plus tests/client/browser-smoke/remapped-pointer.test.ts. 935bf8e itself only adds the read-only movement probe (movement-probe.mjs, movement-probe.test.ts, movement-simulation.test.ts) and the movement/stop assertions in run.mjs, which observe the real pointer command and the real S keydown snapshot and require the stopped and later ticks to stay at the keydown position. Because c1d65ff is 935bf8e's parent, checking out 935bf8e exercised both fixes. No product, renderer or timeout rule changed in this unit.
source.resultBranchRelation: The result branch at 5347117 contains neither c1d65ff nor 935bf8e: `git merge-base --is-ancestor c1d65ff 5347117` and the same check for 935bf8e are both false, because its evidence commits sit on 9df6192 while the fixed runner is on dot-b/playable-backlog-20261028. The receiver must merge the fixed branch (which contains both c1d65ff and 935bf8e), or cherry-pick both c1d65ff and 935bf8e together, while keeping the 02e1aa2 and 5347117 failed-run records, then commit this round's evidence directory. Cherry-picking only 935bf8e is not enough: it would drop c1d65ff, the remapped-pointer mouse return into the current canvas, and the next round's remapped-F targeting and save-refresh-resume smoke could fail again.
